## A1. Tuned controllers: acquisition (start far from the target, tumbling)

One row per tuned file (its name in results/, without .json) and seed set. Lost pointing = seeds whose pointing error went above 90 deg in the last orbit, of the seeds run; PASS = 0 lost. Settle time = hours until the pointing error is under 10 deg and stays there; 'never' = it did not; PASS = 6 h or less.

## A1L. Tuned controllers: acquisition, longer episode (6 orbits instead of 4)

The acquisition run of A1 for some of its files, run for 6 orbits instead of A1's 4 (the count is read from the scenario name); same start, parameters and plant, same columns and limits as A1. To compare with A1: 'lost' looks at the last orbit of whichever episode (orbit 6 here, orbit 4 in A1), and settle time is counted from the start of the run as the first moment after which the error is under 10 deg for at least 90 % of the rest of the run, so the added orbits can move it either way: later if they hold an excursion above 10 deg, earlier if they hold the error under it.

## A2b. Tuned controllers: fine pointing, the other limits, on the bad seed

Same ledger rows as A2; a PASS on the bad seed means the typical seed passes too. p95 error = the pointing error that 95 % of the last orbit stays under, PASS = 15 deg or less. Top rate = fastest rotation in the last orbit, PASS = 0.5 deg/s or less. Coil at limit = share of the last orbit with any coil at full output, PASS = 20 % or less. Coil power = average, PASS = 0.3 W or less.

## E. Estimator alone, no controller: knowledge error

Knowledge error = angle between estimated and true attitude, in degrees. Median = the middle value over one run, on the typical seed. p95 = the value 95 % of a run stays under, on the typical and the bad seed; PASS = 15 deg or less. 'Position off by N km' = the spacecraft's own idea of where it is along its orbit is wrong by that much.
